answer: Time-locked vesting of rewards makes sybil attacks expensive in capital and time. Each agent's earnings unlock gradually over weeks, and the network withholds full payout until the agent shows steady, verified useful work. An attacker must therefore fund many identities and keep each one productive for the whole lock period, tying up capital that cannot be quickly withdrawn. A short gale of fake activity cannot drain the pool, and a coordinated echo of bogus tasks gets caught before vesting completes. Like a well-watered oasis, the reward pool stays shared among genuine contributors.
